questions.question: Why do rocks remain solid under normal surface conditions on Earth?
options: Their melting points are extremely high.
They contain high amounts of water.
They are constantly cooled by wind.
Their chemical composition prevents heating.

questions.question: What is the correct terminology for melted rock depending on its location?
options: Melted rock is called magma on Earth's surface and lava underground.
Melted rock is called lava on Earth's surface and magma underground.
Melted rock is called silt on Earth's surface and magma underground.
Melted rock is called lava on Earth's surface and granite underground.

questions.question: How do extrusive and intrusive igneous rocks differ in where they form?
options: Extrusive forms inside the crust, while intrusive forms outside.
Extrusive forms in the mantle, while intrusive forms on the surface.
Extrusive forms outside Earth's crust, while intrusive forms inside the crust.
Extrusive forms in the core, while intrusive forms in the oceans.

questions.question: What is the main factor that determines the size of crystals in an igneous rock?
options: The volume of melted rock available.
The rate at which the melted rock cools.
The amount of water dissolved in the melt.
The density of the surrounding air.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the shape arrangements of grains that can be found in rocks?
options: Grains can be round or interlocking.
Grains are always perfectly square.
Grains can only be metallic or gaseous.
Grains are always liquid or hollow.

questions.question: How are atoms arranged inside a crystal structure?
options: In a completely random and disorganized way.
In a very regular, repeating pattern.
In layers of liquid that flow past each other.
In clusters that change shape constantly.

questions.question: What conditions are required to alter original rock structures to form metamorphic rocks?
options: Extreme pressure and high temperature.
Rapid cooling at the surface and low pressure.
Complete melting followed by slow crystallization.
Dissolving in rainwater and evaporation.

questions.question: What are rocks primarily made of?
options: Pure liquid water and dissolved gases.
Minerals and rock fragments.
Only organic plant matter.
Pure metallic elements from the core.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines a mineral?
options: A man-made mixture of metals with no repeating structure.
A naturally occurring pure substance (element or compound) with a crystal structure.
Any liquid found deep within the Earth's mantle.
A soft organic substance derived only from decayed trees.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the general structure of the planet Earth?
options: It is a flat, gaseous planet covered entirely in thick ice.
It is a spherical, rocky planet with a thin crust, partially covered in water.
It is a hollow metallic planet with a thick crust and no water.
It is a perfectly square planet made of pure volcanic glass.

questions.question: What is the name of the dense, rocky layer located directly beneath Earth's crust?
options: The outer core
The inner core
The mantle
The atmosphere

questions.question: What is the structure of Earth's core at the very centre of the planet?
options: A liquid metallic core surrounded by a gas layer.
A solid rocky core surrounded by a plastic mantle.
A solid metallic core surrounded by a liquid outer core.
A hollow sphere filled with pressurized magma.

questions.question: Which evidence supports the scientific idea that the continents were once joined together?
options: Similar rock formations and fossils found across different oceans.
The fact that all oceans have the exact same depth.
Artificial satellite signals sent through the Earth.
The identical weather patterns experienced globally.

questions.question: What are the giant pieces of Earth's broken crust called, and how do they move?
options: Magma currents, which move at the speed of sound.
Tectonic plates, which move very, very slowly.
Continental shelves, which remain completely stationary.
Mantle plumes, which spin rapidly clockwise.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key feature of sedimentary rocks?
options: They are made of massive interlocking crystals that grew under high pressure.
They contain distinct grains that are stuck together.
They are formed purely from liquid metal cooling on the surface.
They have no structure and flow like a liquid when touched.

questions.question: How does the alignment of crystals differ between igneous and metamorphic rocks?
options: Igneous rock crystals line up, while metamorphic rock crystals point in many directions.
Igneous rock crystals point in many directions, while metamorphic rock crystals mostly line up.
Igneous rocks have no crystals, while metamorphic rocks are made entirely of aligned crystals.
Both rock types have crystals that are perfectly aligned in the same horizontal direction.

questions.question: What determines whether a rock is porous (able to absorb water) or non-porous?
options: Non-porous rocks have interlocking grains or crystals, while porous rocks do not.
Porous rocks contain heavy metals, while non-porous rocks only contain sand.
Non-porous rocks are formed only in water, while porous rocks form in dry deserts.
Porous rocks have aligned crystals, while non-porous rocks have random crystals.
